title: A 91-Year-Old Just Hiked 2,198 Miles — and Set a Record
summary:
Imagine walking from Georgia to Maine. Now imagine doing it at 91 years old.

On August 31, 2026, Dale Sanders finished the Appalachian Trail, a 2,198-mile path through forests and rocky mountains. At 91, he became the oldest person ever to complete it. His nickname? "Grey Beard."

Sanders hiked for 359 days, about 12 miles a day, with one rest day each week. He started in West Virginia so he could see Georgia's colorful fall leaves, then took a break during the snowy winter.

It wasn't easy. He fell 71 times! Once, in Vermont, he tumbled into a pile of boulders and scraped his legs, arms, and hands. Later, his arm went numb, and doctors worried he'd had a stroke. It turned out to be a pinched nerve.

Near the very end, just 1,000 feet from the top of Mount Katahdin, he fell again. He lay there a moment — then got up and kept climbing.

This isn't even his first record. He first became the oldest AT hiker in 2017, at 82. His friend broke that record in 2021 — so Sanders decided to take it back. "You just have to want to do it," he says.
why_it_matters: It shows kids that big goals — like a long school project or learning a new skill — get finished by showing up again and again, not by being fast or young.

background_read: People who hike a whole long trail in one trip are called "thru-hikers." Every year, thousands of people try to walk the entire Appalachian Trail, but only a small share of them make it all the way to Maine.
The Appalachian Trail ends at the top of Mount Katahdin (the highest mountain in Maine), and it is one of the longest marked hiking paths in the world.
Other long trails, like the Pacific Crest Trail on the West Coast, also have hikers trying to set "oldest person" records.
Article_Structure: WHO: Dale Sanders, a 91-year-old hiker nicknamed "Grey Beard," who finished the Appalachian Trail on August 31, 2026.
WHAT: He completed the 2,198-mile trail and became the oldest person ever to do it, hiking 359 days at about 12 miles a day.
WHERE: The Appalachian Trail from Georgia to Maine — he started in West Virginia and finished near the top of Mount Katahdin.
WHY: He wanted the record back after his friend broke it in 2021, and he says, "You just have to want to do it."

perspectives.description: Some people see Sanders as proof that you are never too old for a huge adventure, and that falling down is just part of the trip.
Others might point out that falling 71 times is a lot, especially for someone 91 years old, and that he was lucky not to be hurt worse.
Records like this change hands often — his friend took it in 2021 and he took it back — so the real story may be his stubbornness, not the title.
